seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the sharp expected-sup minimax risk under a common vanishing boundary tube-mass modulus.
seed_details.summary: Show that the scalar common modulus is insufficient by constructing isolated and pervasive thinning classes with the same \(h^{\kappa}\) modulus but different minimax rates, then introduce \(\mathsf J_P\) as the corrected focal object.
seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction and Conclusion frame the whole-boundary target; Theorem 4 uses a regular \(h^2\) stochastic scale; Theorem 6 and Supplemental Appendix Section SA-8.35 build a two-sector pointwise lower experiment, not a multiplicity-sensitive thinning family.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed positive-Gram maximal inequality by local-variance chaining indexed jointly by boundary location and thin-site multiplicity, and replace the two-point lower bound by legal boundary packings with controlled support geometry.
seed_details.red_team: Gaiffas2009Uniform already shows that isolated density zeros behave differently, so the result is immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: That paper has a one-dimensional regression design and no same-common-modulus two-geometry theorem, two assignment sides, causal curve, or sufficient boundary packing profile.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct a boundary CATE estimator selected from empirical one-sided counts and match its uniform oracle risk under unknown thickness.
seed_details.summary: Prove a same-class adaptive upper and Fano lower rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when polynomially thin sites are pervasive.
seed_details.anchor_read: Sections 2--3 construct the stabilized local-polynomial Lepski selector and Theorem 2 gives pointwise adaptation; the first boundary change is uniform two-side count control over a continuum.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn one empirical interval count and one Gram matrix into two one-sided ball counts uniformly over \((x,h)\), using local constants so count positivity is the only inversion issue.
seed_details.red_team: The rate is Gaiffas's pointwise polynomial-degeneracy formula with a logarithm inserted.
seed_details.rebuttal: The logarithm must be earned by a legal \(h^{-1}\)-site causal packing, and the estimator must adapt simultaneously over boundary locations and both assignment sides.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine whether honest variable-width bands can adapt to unknown boundary thickness and characterize the necessary separation condition if not.
seed_details.summary: Derive a thickness-indexed honest-width lower bound and a conditionally calibrated count-adaptive band attaining it.
seed_details.anchor_read: Theorems 2.1--2.2 derive honest scalar bias-aware intervals from an ordered-modulus calculation; CTY Theorem 5 and CCK Theorem 3.1 provide the boundary and Gaussian-supremum components to rebuild under thinning.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Establish conditional Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration when the selected local count and studentizing variance both vary toward zero along the boundary.
seed_details.red_team: CCK already permits data-selected resolutions and multiplier bands.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its generic theorem does not verify two vanishing signed-side denominators, random local Gram scales, or a thickness-specific expected-width lower bound.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the exact consistency frontier for arbitrary declared moduli.
seed_details.summary: Use triangular moduli and thickness entropy to make the effective-sample-size criterion nontrivial.
seed_details.anchor_read: Theorem 2 proves logarithmically slow pointwise consistency under severe fixed density degeneracy, showing that a fixed-positive-modulus order-one claim is false.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a fixed design density by a triangular boundary design and prove necessity through a same-row legal packing.
seed_details.red_team: The criterion is a tautological restatement of effective sample size.
seed_details.rebuttal: It is tautological for a fixed positive scalar modulus, but necessity and data-driven sufficiency are substantive for deteriorating thickness--entropy profiles.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Derive uniform inference for a selected signed-distance bandwidth under vanishing local mass.
seed_details.summary: Express a conditional Gaussian approximation error in the realized minimum one-sided count and determine the necessity boundary for bootstrap validity.
seed_details.anchor_read: Theorem 5 and Supplemental Appendix Theorems SA-7--SA-9 rely on normalized Gram eigenvalues bounded away from zero and a fixed bandwidth.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Track the inverse-count envelope through strong approximation over the random location--bandwidth index.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a technical restatement of the CCK coupling theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The load-bearing work is the primitive verification and failure boundary under two-side thinning, which neither CCK nor CTY supplies.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Translate primitive support geometry and density into signed-distance local-polynomial Gram coercivity.
seed_details.summary: Characterize the radial-balance condition under which a mass modulus controls every local-polynomial moment eigenvalue.
seed_details.anchor_read: The banked reviewers explicitly reject identifying total local mass with Gram coercivity; CTY Supplemental Lemma SA-2 gives only a regular positive-density sufficient condition.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Derive moment-matrix eigenvalue bounds from subannulus mass rather than total ball mass.
seed_details.red_team: For the Lipschitz target, local constants avoid the Gram issue entirely.
seed_details.rebuttal: That is why this is not the selected kernel, but the theorem remains necessary for higher-order extensions used by existing software.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Use a thickness-adaptive BATEC to choose treatment for a boundary-marginal population.
seed_details.summary: Prove a margin-localized regret oracle for a policy on \(\mathcal B\), potentially avoiding the worst-location uniform rate when thin regions carry little policy weight.
seed_details.anchor_read: The CTY supplemental extensions define weighted and largest boundary effects, while Luedtke and Chambaz give a generic plug-in policy regret conversion under ordinary treatment overlap.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a global sup event by a thickness-weighted disagreement process and preserve deterministic two-side identification in the lower family.
seed_details.red_team: The policy upper bound follows immediately from a sup-norm CATE rate and a margin condition.
seed_details.rebuttal: Only the crude fallback does; an integrated local-information oracle and same-class lower bound are not supplied by either source.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Characterize policy-relevant functionals of the BATEC when design density vanishes at the boundary.
seed_details.summary: Derive the first nonzero welfare variation under a normal deformation of the treatment boundary when ordinary first-order mass vanishes.
seed_details.anchor_read: CTY motivates policy-relevant boundary functionals but does not study deformation; the destination search found only regular-density submanifold integral calculus.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the ordinary linear tube formula by a uniform regularly varying weighted tube formula.
seed_details.red_team: This is Reynolds transport with a different scaling.
seed_details.rebuttal: The ordinary derivative is zero under vanishing density; the nonzero \(\kappa\)-order signed derivative and its learnability are new objects.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Derive an efficiency bound for the unsmoothed boundary CATE curve under thinning.
seed_details.summary: Search for a classical efficient influence function for the pointwise or sup-norm BATEC.
seed_details.anchor_read: The target is a conditional mean at a continuously distributed boundary point, so its formal Dirac score is not square-integrable.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A pathwise derivative would need an \(L^2(P)\) Riesz representer, which does not exist for the unsmoothed point target.
seed_details.red_team: The efficiency bound is infinite because the estimand is nonregular.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; this lane was dropped and replaced by the honest-width ordered-modulus seed.

seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Obtain boundary-wide causal coverage by permutation or conformal inversion.
seed_details.summary: Search for a finite-sample symmetry orbit compatible with deterministic boundary assignment and varying local thickness.
seed_details.anchor_read: The exact-validity theorem requires exchangeable residuals and a permutation-invariant null fit; approximate validity uses stationary weak dependence.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: No side-exchangeability action preserves the sharp boundary RD law under continuity alone.
seed_details.red_team: A conformal band would require adding a local-randomization assignment model or would cover outcomes rather than the conditional mean curve.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so the M17 lane was dropped rather than padded into the proposal.

literature_map.anchor: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance, Introduction, Theorems 4--6, Conclusion, and Supplemental Appendix Section SA-8.35, fixes the causal target and regular-thickness proof architecture but excludes vanishing density through its density and Gram assumptions.
adjacent_threads: Gaiffas2005Degenerate, Theorems 1--2 and Section 3, supplies the pointwise bias--local-mass equation, stabilized estimator, and least-favorable bumps for regular and severe degeneracy.
Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive, Sections 2--4, supplies empirical-design Lepski selection and the adaptive lower-bound logic at one query point.
Gaiffas2009Uniform, equation (2.1), Theorems 1--2, and Proposition 1, is the closest generic-regression comparator and shows why isolated versus pervasive thinning must be distinguished.
Kpotufe2011LocalDimension supplies a neighbor-radius device for adaptation to unknown local ball mass under doubling measures.
ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest, Theorems 2.1--2.2, supply the anti-concentration and honest-width templates for the open inference node.
The M11(b) search found no finite classical efficiency bound for the unsmoothed pointwise BATEC because the conditional mean at a continuously distributed point is nonregular.
The M17 search found no symmetry orbit under deterministic boundary assignment; the exact conformal comparator requires exchangeability absent from the continuity model.
